# Exercise R4: Discriminant in the Ideal Generated by $f$ and $f'$

## Problem Statement

> [!question] Exercise
> Let $f=ax^2+bx+c$, with $a,b,c$ in a ring $R$. Show that the ideal of $R[x]$ generated by $f$ and $f'$ contains the discriminant, the constant polynomial $b^2-4ac$.

## Hints

> [!hint]- Hint 1
> Compute $f'=2ax+b$.

> [!hint]- Hint 2
> Expand $(f')^2-4af$.

## Solution

> [!success]- Solution
> In $R[x]$,
> $$
> f'=2ax+b.
> $$
> Therefore
> $$
> (f')^2-4af
> =(2ax+b)^2-4a(ax^2+bx+c)
> =b^2-4ac.
> $$
> The first term is $f'\cdot f'$ and the second is $f\cdot(-4a)$. Hence
> $$
> b^2-4ac=(-4a)f+f'f'\in(f,f').
> $$
> This identity is valid in any commutative ring, including characteristics $2$ and $3$.

## Notes

The statement is from S1; the displayed ideal identity is independently derived and requires no division by $2$ or by $a$.
